card: Handles block and undo file write errors explicitly so disk write failures (such as running out of disk space) trigger a clean fatal shutdown with diagnostic logs instead of crashing via std::terminate. In BufferedWriter, pending bytes are cleared before writing to avoid destructor re-throws during exception unwinding, a discard() method abandons pending bytes on write failure, and an Assume assertion ensures buffers are emptied before destruction. This fixes a crash regression introduced in #31551 when buffered writing was added.
changed_since_previous: Added an explicit `discard()` method to `BufferedWriter` to drop pending bytes on failure, and extended writer scope in block and undo file writing to discard buffers before closing files.
evidence: Author notes encountering the issue regularly: "my 1 TB benchmarking servers have recently been filling up, so I've been seeing these failures more often."
Author identifies the regression origin: "I introduced this bug in #31551 when adding `BufferedWriter`."

Author provides a minimal sed-based reproducer demonstrating an immediate crash via `std::terminate` without clean shutdown before the patch, and graceful exit status 1 with diagnostic logs after the patch.
problem: When disk writes fail (such as when a disk fills up during block or undo writes), `AutoFile::write_buffer()` throws `std::ios_base::failure`. Because `BufferedWriter`'s destructor was implicitly non-throwing, unflushed buffer exceptions in the destructor triggered an abrupt `std::terminate` crash instead of a graceful shutdown, and failed flushes left pending bytes that caused the destructor to attempt re-writing while an exception was already unwinding.

risk.why: Alters error handling and buffering during block and undo file writes, where a bug could mishandle disk I/O errors or leave partially written data unclosed.

summary: Flushes buffered block and undo data explicitly before destruction, catching write exceptions to log them, close the file, and trigger a clean fatal shutdown. In `BufferedWriter`, clears pending bytes before writing so failed flushes do not re-throw during exception unwinding, provides an explicit `discard()` method on errors, and asserts empty buffers on destruction with `Assume`.
